qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Lecture sixteen. Hardware software co-design: chips and code made for each other.
Meet Leafly. Snap a photo of a leaf, and it names the plant.
Leafly: snap a leaf, get the plant's name.
Today the photo goes to a server. The answer takes seconds, and with no signal there is none.
Today the photo goes to the cloud. Answer: a few seconds.
AI pushes general chips to their limits. A Swiss army knife does everything, a garlic press does one job far better.
AI pushes general hardware to its limits.
And chips no longer get faster on their own. Moore's law is slowing.
Moore's law is slowing: waiting won't do it.
A new chip is very expensive, so it needs a large demand. AI has one.
A new chip is very expensive, so it needs large demand.
Hardware first. A chip is designed around the software it will run.
Hardware designed around the software it will run.
Then software. A model or a library is tuned to use that chip, sometimes before it even exists.
Software tuned to make full use of that hardware.
Each shapes the other. That is hardware software co-design.
Both shaped by each other: hardware–software co-design.
AI models run on tensor operations, big grids of numbers.
AI models run on tensor operations.
Images fill the grid, so they use dense tensors. Recommendations are mostly empty, so they use sparse ones.
Images: dense tensors. Recommendations: sparse ones.
Most AI still runs in the cloud, far from the user.
AI usually runs in the cloud.
As models get personal, the work moves onto the phone. That is edge computing.
Personal models move it onto the phone: edge computing.
In cars, driver assistance chips turn camera images into braking within milliseconds.
Cars: ADAS chips see the road and brake in milliseconds.
In data centres, D P Us and I P Us sit beside the server's CPU.
Data centres: DPUs and IPUs sit beside the CPU.
They take networking, storage and security, so the CPU can run the customer's work.
They take networking, storage and security off its hands.
Bottom-up: the hardware comes first, the software later. Early GPU computing worked like that.
Bottom-up: hardware first, software later. Early GPU computing.
Top-down: the workload drives a new chip. Volta tensor cores were built for AI.
Top-down: the workload drives the chip. Volta tensor cores.
Co-design: both are designed together, as in Snapdragon Ride Flex and Ride Vision.
Co-design: both together. Snapdragon Ride Flex and Ride Vision.
Demand drives software, software drives hardware, and the loop goes round again.
Demand, software, hardware, round again: an iterative loop.
Partitioning decides which jobs go into hardware. Leafly has six.
Six Leafly jobs. Which go into hardware?
The heavy, stable ones move over, and gain speed and parallelism.
Heavy, stable jobs to hardware: speed and parallelism.
Pet safety rules change often. In silicon they would need a new chip, so they stay in software.
Rules that change stay in software, easy to update.
Engineers simulate a model of the chip together with the real code, before building anything.
Simulate chip and code together before building anything.
With high level synthesis, they describe the behaviour and a tool produces the hardware design.
High-level synthesis: describe the behaviour, get an HDL design.
Profile first. On the phone's CPU, one photo takes a hundred and thirty-two milliseconds.
One photo on the phone's CPU: 132 ms.
The network alone takes a hundred and twenty.
The network takes 120 of them.
On the GPU the photo takes forty milliseconds, but thirteen of those are copying.
Network on the GPU: 40 ms, but 13 ms of it is copying.
A GPU twice as fast only shrinks the network bar. Thirty-two and a half.
A GPU twice as fast: only 32.5 ms.
With a photo four times as big, the copies take fifty-two milliseconds. Moving data can cost more than computing.
A photo 4 times as big: copies take 52 ms.
A CPU suits varied tasks, a GPU parallel maths, and a specialised chip stable, frequent work.
CPU: varied tasks. GPU: maths in parallel. Specialised: stable work.
The photo is passed on like a baton: CPU, then GPU, then CPU again.
CPU prepares, GPU runs the network, CPU shows the answer.
The framework, the compiler and the runtime map the model onto the chip.
Framework, compiler, runtime: the stack maps the model to the chip.
Measure latency, throughput, energy per result and cost.
Measure latency, throughput, energy per result and cost.
Prototype, measure the whole pipeline, and revisit the partition.
Prototype, measure end to end, revisit the partition.
Speed one part up, and the bottleneck moves, often to copying.
Speed one part up and the bottleneck moves.
Co-design trades power, performance, cost and development time, in phones, cars and five G.
Co-design trades power, performance, cost and time.
The chip is shaped by the software, and the software by the chip.
Heavy, stable jobs go into hardware. Anything that changes stays in software.
Profile, watch the copies, and measure the whole pipeline.
